description:
FILED s530c (Opus agent, 2026-10-31).  PRE-EXISTING (base 0fb05a79 gives the same).  Found when #3859 let Pod-Simple t/fcodes_s.t run past its old stop: its rows 13-34 (Pod::Simple::Text output) now RUN and fail on this.

    use Text::Wrap; local $Text::Wrap::huge = 'overflow';
    my $o = Text::Wrap::wrap("  ", "  ", "abc\n"); $o =~ s/\n/\\n/g; print "[$o]\n";
  perl 5.40.3: [  abc\n]        PCL: [  abc]          (also "abc def\nghi\n" -> PCL drops the LAST newline only)
Probe scratch/s530c/pr/wrap1.pl.  Pod::Simple::Text::emit_par is `wrap($indent, $indent, $self->{'Thispara'} .= "\n")` + print "\n", so every paragraph ends "\n" where perl's ends "\n\n".

NARROWED (scratch/s530c/pr/wrap2-4.pl, all IDENTICAL to perl): the two regexes of wrap()'s loop with their captures and pos, the loop itself replicated in a script (`while ($t !~ /\G(?:$break)*\Z/gc) {...} $r .= $remainder` gives "  abc\n" under PCL too), Text::Tabs::expand("abc\n"), the map/join that builds $t.  So the difference is in what the transpiled core Text/Wrap.pm does that the replica does not: candidates `use re 'taint'` in the sub, the `local $Text::Wrap::huge` read through the package global, `$lead`/`$nl` initialisation, or the `pos($t) ne length($t)` tail.  Next step: transpile Text/Wrap.pm (`./pl2cl --module`) and bisect by copying wrap() into a script.
ROWS: Pod-Simple-3.47 t/fcodes_s.t rows 13-34 (22 rows, blessed to this task by s530c).

=== DISSOLVED (s531c, 2026-11-01): the primitive is #932 -- capture variables are not dynamically scoped ===
REDUCED: wrap()'s loop does `$r .= $unexpand ? unexpand($nl . $lead . $1) : ...; $remainder = $2;` -- Text::Tabs::unexpand runs its OWN matches, and PCL's $2 after the call is unexpand's (empty), where perl restores the caller's $2 when unexpand's scope exits.  So `$remainder` is "" instead of "\n" and the last newline is lost.  Proof: the same core Text/Wrap.pm copied as WrapCopy.pm (scratch/s531c/p/) with `$WrapCopy::unexpand = 0` gives "  abc\n" = perl under PCL; with the default 1 it gives "  abc".  The s530c replica agreed with perl because it did not call unexpand.
Primitive probe (scratch/s531c/p/cap1.pl), perl 5.40.3 vs s531c tree:
    sub f { "xyz" =~ /(y)/; "f$1" }  "abc" =~ /(b)(c)/; my $r = f(); print "$1 $2 $r"      perl: b c fy     PCL: y  fy
    "m1" =~ /(m)/; { "n2" =~ /(n)/ } print $1                                          perl: m          PCL: n
That is #932 word for word (pending since s461ar, its fix shape and cost note unchanged).  Not fixed here: #932 is a per-scope save/restore of the whole match record ($1..$20 are eager specials, *match-rs* / *match-re* are REUSED vectors mutated in place), a design on the hottest path whose cost the task itself says must be measured first -- not one mechanism inside one layer.
ROWS: Pod-Simple-3.47 t/fcodes_s.t rows 13-34 (22) re-caused from #4103 to #932 by edit in baselines/cpan-board14-fails.tsv (s531c).
subject: Text::Wrap::wrap drops the LAST trailing newline of its text (`wrap("  ","  ","abc\n")` is "  abc" where perl gives "  abc\n") -- silent wrong; every Pod::Simple::Text paragraph ends one newline short (Pod-Simple fcodes_s.t rows 13-34)
